html:
On 27 July 1990 the Jamaat al Muslimeen, a Black Muslim group led by Yasin Abu Bakr, tried to overthrow the government of Trinidad and Tobago. Gunmen stormed Parliament and the state television station.

They held Prime Minister A. N. R. Robinson and members of his cabinet hostage for six days; Robinson was shot in the leg. Looting broke out in Port of Spain, and about two dozen people died.

The rebels surrendered after being promised an amnesty. The attempt remains the only Islamist armed attempt to seize power in the Americas, and it scarred a country proud of its stable democracy since Eric Williams and the crisis of 1970.
sum: On 27 July 1990 the Jamaat al Muslimeen, a Black Muslim group led by Yasin Abu Bakr, tried to overthrow the government of Trinidad and Tobago. Gunmen stormed Parliament and the state television station.
